task: Replace name-sensitive generic lowering and verify the accepted diagnostic on a generic raising call.
observation: The backend skipped generic classification for any function whose name contained the word 'generic', even when SemanticChecker had marked its signature generic. Removing the name test made the generic_score function use the macro lowering path. A focused structured differential also found Java reported an escaping typed error at the call expression while C++ reports the main declaration line.
impact: Function naming affected generated Rust selection, and the structured differential exposed a precise diagnostic location mismatch without invoking native acceptance. Using checker facts and the main declaration location produced stable, source-backed decisions.

resolution.summary: Generic lowering now uses checker/type facts rather than the function name, and escaping typed errors from main use the same diagnostic line as C++. Focused generated-Rust inspection and the three-file structured differential pass.
